To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the least squares disclosure attacks (LSDA) is a powerful tool for deanonymization of traffic through mixes and that its success is characterized by the system parameters.
LSDA (i) is the first disclosure attack that allows to analytically determine the profiling accuracy, (ii) is more accurate than previous attacks and (iii) works well with pool mixes.

LSDA (a) is a general attack that can be easily adapted to analyze different mix designs; (b) is more accurate than previous attacks; and (c) allows us to analyzably characterize its performance with respect to the network parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the static traffic analysis of high-latency anonymity systems, and we believe that the LSDA will be useful to both the design of new anonymity systems as well as the analysis of existing ones.
